zip_caveats: Long Beach's own races were all settled in June: Mayor Rex Richardson, City Auditor Laura Doud and the council members for Districts 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 won outright, and the city attorney and city prosecutor ran unopposed. Long Beach Unified's three school board seats were settled in June too, and there is no Long Beach city or school measure this time. So a Long Beach ballot holds the state races, LA County's races and Measures A and E, your district races, and, for some voters, a city college trustee and a water board seat. ZIPs: 90810 is about half Carson and touches the City of LA, and 90755 is almost all Signal Hill, a separate city in the middle of Long Beach, so the guide asks which city you live in. Signal Hill also reaches small parts of 90804 and 90806. 90813 is mostly Long Beach, with a small part in the City of LA near the harbor. Districts: most of Long Beach is in Congressional District 42; North Long Beach (90805) and most of West Long Beach (90810) are in District 44; and much of 90808 in east Long Beach, next to Lakewood, is in District 41. Most of the city is in Assembly District 69; North Long Beach, mostly in 90805, is in District 65. All of Long Beach is in State Senate District 33, which doesn't vote this year, so there is no State Senate race here. Only Long Beach City College Trustee Area 5 (much of East Long Beach north of the 405, plus California Heights) votes for a college trustee this year. Almost all of the city is in Water Replenishment District Division 3; a small corner of North Long Beach is in Division 5, which doesn't vote this year. A few edge blocks are in Paramount, ABC or Compton Unified instead of Long Beach Unified; any races for those boards are not in this guide. Your address lookup, or your official sample ballot at isb.lavote.gov, shows your exact races.

situations.short: Get a replacement at any LA County vote center or just vote there.
situations.answer: The last day to ask for a ballot by mail was October 27. You can still go to any LA County vote center and ask for a replacement or vote there in person. Questions? Call (800) 815-2666, press 2, then 3.
steps: Use the county's locator to find a vote center near you.

notes: You can vote at any LA County vote center, in Long Beach or anywhere else in the county; the county's locator shows wait times. Long Beach has 20 county ballot drop boxes, open around the clock until 8 PM on November 3, including at City Hall, neighborhood libraries, park community centers and Cal State Long Beach.
